store_read.second_reading: the original: silver/transactions/ day files in opal-data-bd, current bytes (newest day with rows in 2026-10)

sweep_test.note: the name test found no sweep or reinvest-labelled Buy in either store; the Buy type itself carries no sub-type other than Buy, and reinvested income sits under its own type (Dividend Reinvestment), which the rule excludes. A sweep fund whose name matches none of the listed words would still count as a purchase: a stated limit

what_it_cannot_say: A same-day purchase does not show the custodian counted the cash from the start of the day.
The count describes these accounts' trading, not either system's method of timing a flow.

A purchase dated on or after a deposit may have been paid from cash already in the account or from a sale; the data does not tag cash to a purchase, so 'first invested' is the first sizeable purchase, not proof of what funded it.
Twelve days where cash may have arrived as a transfer in are not counted as deposit days (other days); the data does not tell an in-kind transfer from a cash one.
It does not say which convention (START, MID or END) is right; 47 of the 51 segments close under START and MID alike and none under END, and nothing here changes that.
limits: Sweep funds are found by name and sub-type only; none were found, so any sweep fund not matching those words would be counted as a purchase and would pull a deposit toward same_day or next_trading_day.
A purchase after a later flow-bearing day of the same account is still attributed to the earlier deposit (8 deposit days).
The 10 percent size threshold is a choice; a different share would move days between the classes.
Never_in_window means no purchase of at least a tenth of the deposit by trade date inside the segment window; smaller buys or buys filed under a different type are not seen.
The standing-plan figure is a proxy.

the_39.statement: 39 of the 90 two-sided segments close under NO timing (31 of the accrual class, 8 unclassed); nothing in this record changes them, and a change of flow-timing convention would not close the tie-out.
